notes.775: atich is taken as dwarf elder, ebech as ivy, storchessnabel as cranesbill (Geranium), berhtram as pellitory. mitewirz is unidentified. 'in deme drîetage' is read as 'for three days'; it could be 'on the third day'.

nodes.text: If any man or woman becomes palsied on the right side,
then let blood from him in the left hand, at the
ball of the little finger, and at the ball of the little
toe of the right foot. But if it is on his left
side, then let blood from him in the right hand, at
the ball of the little finger, and at the ball of the left
little toe. After that, take oats, threshed
and unthreshed, and dwarf elder, and ivy, and
fern, and ants, and wormwood, and stinging nettles,
and make a bath, and bathe him in it for three days.
And then take ginger, wine and honey, and
leaves of the white willow, and cherry-tree leaves, and
peach-tree leaves, and sage, and rue, and cranesbill,
one ounce by weight, and make a drink, and [let him] drink
it in the warm bath; then he will be cured of it.
